_comment: Two independent trees. (1) years -> semesters -> subjects -> items: a subject is a folder (e.g. assets/guides/year-1/sem-1/cc104/); subject shape {id, code, title, items: []}. Each item is one of four kinds: {id, kind:"week", label, order, week, html?, pdf?, pptx?, docx?, xlsx?} (numbered week), {id, kind:"special", label, order, html?, pdf?, pptx?, docx?, xlsx?} (freeform entry like a Midterm Reviewer), {id, kind:"note", label, order, text} (markdown text stored inline, no file at all), or {id, kind:"link", label, order, url} (an external URL embedded directly in the viewer — whether the target site actually allows that is up to the site itself, GitHub Pages can't control it; 'Open in new tab' is the fallback either way). html/pdf/pptx/docx/xlsx are all optional paths relative to this file, an item can carry any combination of them (the viewer shows a format-toggle button per one present) — a week/special item needs at least one, a note needs `text` instead and never has any of them, a link needs `url` instead and never has any of them either. PPTX/DOCX/XLSX render through Microsoft's free Office Online viewer (needs the file to be at a public URL, which GitHub Pages already gives it) and are always directly downloadable regardless. (2) references -> items: general material not tied to any year/semester/subject (e.g. assets/references/web-development/); category shape {id, label, items: []}, each item {id, title, order, kind:"doc"|"note"|"link", html?/pdf?/pptx?/docx?/xlsx? for kind:"doc", text? for kind:"note", url? for kind:"link"} — same kind split and multi-format support as subject items, just without the week/special distinction. Both trees start empty — publish from /admin.html and entries land here automatically. order controls sidebar/library sort order in both trees. Nothing in script.js needs to change when subjects, items, or reference categories are added — manual editing works too.
